title: Credit Builder Accounts Late Fee Amount
content:
The late fee on a Credit Builder Accounts plan is the plan's late-fee percent of the plan's monthly payment, not more than the plan's late-fee maximum, rounded to the cent.

## How the figure is reached

1. The late due date is the account's oldest unpaid due date, the next due date the account shows; the fee is figured for that due date.
2. The fee is the plan's late-fee percent applied to the plan's monthly payment, worked without rounding.
3. The fee is rounded to the nearest cent once, as the last arithmetic step, a half cent or more rounding up; every rounding to the cent on a Credit Builder late fee goes to the nearest cent in that way.
4. The rounded fee is then held to the plan's late-fee maximum: a fee above the maximum is charged at the maximum.

A late fee that comes to 0.00 is not charged, and the late due date then needs no late fee; nothing is charged when the late due date already carries its late fee. Whether it carries one is read from the account's late-fee entries, each tied to the due date it was charged for.

The plan's late-fee percent, late-fee maximum and monthly payment are the figures in the Credit Builder Accounts fee schedule and plan schedule for the account's plan.

## Worked figures (hypothetical schedule figures)

The figures below use invented schedule values, not any plan's real ones: a late-fee percent of 4.0 and a late-fee maximum of 10.00.

| Monthly payment | Percent applied | Rounded | Held to the maximum | Late fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100.00 | 4.00 | 4.00 | 4.00 | 4.00 |
| 112.40 | 4.496 | 4.50 | 4.50 | 4.50 |
| 300.00 | 12.00 | 12.00 | 10.00 | 10.00 |

| Late due date already carries a late fee? | Charge |
|---|---|
| yes | nothing |
| no | the fee figured as above, unless it comes to 0.00 |
